claims.statement: The fragment locates Single sign-on configuration under Identity Provider. This is navigation, not active SSO, protocol selection, enforced authentication, admin entitlement or recovery proof.

The custom-role start sequence uses inspected enterprise and People navigation includes, then Enterprise roles, Role management and Create custom role. It does not provide the role permissions, save/assignment process or actor prerequisites and is not a completed role grant. The enterprise include distinguishes GHES settings navigation from other enterprise access.

In the GHEC branch, opening, viewing and commenting on enterprise-associated support tickets requires enterprise support entitlement. Enterprise owners and billing managers receive it automatically, and owners can grant it to enterprise members. The note separately allows any organization member to create tickets associated with their enterprise-owned organization; that exception does not grant enterprise-ticket access or unrestricted access to other organization tickets. The full linked guide is not reviewed and no ticket or entitlement was changed.

In the GHEC branch, enabling enterprise team synchronization overrides organization-level synchronization settings for enterprise-owned organizations. This precedence caveat is not a verified synchronization event, safe migration guarantee or applicability to the separate EMU SCIM mechanism. The linked guide is not reviewed and no sync setting changed.

Selecting an Azure subscription requires subscription-owner permissions; a different tenant ID may be needed if the default tenant lacks proper permissions. Tenant selection is not privilege escalation or consent approval and does not prove subscription ownership or billing authority for this agent. Linked billing and Microsoft authorization-flow pages are not reviewed; no subscription or tenant connection changed.

The Settings entry Verified and approved domains is a navigation pointer. Verified ownership and approved notification domains remain distinct; the menu label does not prove DNS verification, recipient trust, configured restrictions or authority to change domains.
